column1: # install-parity-allowlist.tsv - reviewed divergences between the twins (SPEC D-ALLOW).
# Nine TAB-separated fields: id, pairs, scenario, path, kind, host, tracker, match, reason.
# A row covers a divergence only for its pair, scenario, path, kind and host; for kind lines every differing
# line must match the match regex of one covering row. Every row has a tracker: accepted (by design) or a
# follow-up id. A row that covers nothing for one of its pairs on a whole-tier run is stale and fails the run.
# A missing row with a fu- tracker may take ? as match: intermittent, it covers when present and is never stale.
# A lines row needs a regex (never -); a regex led by = is paired: its capture group 1 must be equal on both sides.

column9: on a host whose sed is BSD (macOS) sh writes two spaces after Template version: where ps1 writes one (BSD sed reads \s as a literal s; GNU sed strips the space, so the twins agree on Linux and Windows); the match is paired (leading =), so the version value must be the same in both twins and a wrong version on either twin stays visible
ps1 stamps Synced at with seven fraction digits where sh stamps to the second (N1 rewrites only the second-precision shape; the self pair shows two ps1 runs differ by their stamps)

ps1 lays the AAI blocks out in a different order with 4 more blank separator lines; the run shows it as a lines divergence (the files also differ in header text, so the order-only kind never fires, seed kind order corrected to lines)

column8: ^# AAI (runtime sidecars \(seeded (from \.aai/system/RUNTIME_IGNORE\.list|by aai-sync\.ps1); per-dev, never commit\)|runtime reports \(ephemeral; not project-owned docs\)|per-dev runtime state \(RFC-0001: never committed\))\r?$
column9: the runtime sidecar block header names RUNTIME_IGNORE.list in sh and aai-sync.ps1 in ps1, and ps1 adds two more block header comments sh does not write
sh leaves hooks/session-start.sh executable, ps1 does not (PowerShell copies carry no mode bits on POSIX)

sh stamps the sync-conflicts report name in UTC and ps1 in local time, so on a non-UTC host the ps1 name disagrees with its Generated-at line; the driver pairs the two reports by ordinal (their content is compared) and reports the name disagreement alone, at the path ending #name, which is all this row covers
ps1 stamps the report Generated-at line with seven fraction digits, visible on every host now that reports are paired by ordinal
step 2 of HK-09 is the uninstall, which removes the hooks step 1 installed; the self pair therefore differs by design
step 2 of SY-06 syncs the core profile over an extended install, which prunes the extended-only files step 1 wrote; the self pair differs by design
the pin records the profile, which step 2 of SY-06 changes by design
the pruning sync of SY-06 step 2 writes a sync-conflicts report step 1 did not; the self pair differs by design

column8: ^(1\. Inspect each item with \x60?git diff -- <path>\x60? in the target project\.|2\. Ask AI to extract project-specific guidance and place it into project-owned docs \(for example \x60?docs/ai/project-overrides/\x60?\)\.)$
column9: ps1 writes the two next-step lines of the sync-conflicts report without the backticks sh writes around the command and the path; only those two lines, in either spelling, are covered

on Windows the sh twin (Git Bash) records the source path in the POSIX spelling /c/... and the ps1 twin records C:\... for the same directory; only a path under an aai-parity-* scratch directory ending in fx/src is covered, in either spelling; the regex cannot compare the two spellings with each other, so the scratch directory itself is not checked for equality between the twins

the sync-conflicts report names the source path in the Git Bash spelling /c/... in sh and C:\... in ps1 on Windows; only a path under an aai-parity-* scratch directory ending in fx/src is covered, in either spelling, not equality between the twins

on Windows ps1 writes AAI_PIN.md through Set-Content, which ends its last line with CRLF and, under Windows PowerShell 5.1, starts the file with a UTF-8 byte order mark; sh writes LF and no mark; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR and a leading mark are ignored

on Windows ps1 writes the sync-conflicts report with CRLF line ends and, under Windows PowerShell 5.1, a UTF-8 byte order mark; sh writes LF and no mark; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR and a leading mark are ignored

on Windows ps1 appends its .gitignore blocks with Add-Content, which ends each value with CRLF where sh writes LF; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR is ignored

on Windows the sh twin's update leaves empty root directories of the target whose names are random wide characters (three or four per run, born in the last seconds of the step, while the doctor field report runs) and the ps1 twin leaves none; the driver reports each at the path <odd-root-name> with its real name in the detail, and this row covers those entries of the update scenario on a Windows host only
